cards.explanation: The answer is rich generosity. Paul says the Macedonians' "…abundant joy and deep poverty overflowed into rich generosity." (2 Corinthians 8:2) Think about that, friends. Deep poverty and a terrible ordeal, and the giving still came pouring out.

The answer is False. Paul says, "…they gave according to their ability and even beyond it." (2 Corinthians 8:3) They went past what they could afford. And Paul says they did it "Of their own accord…" so nobody had to twist an arm.

The answer is privilege. The Macedonians begged for "…the privilege of sharing in this service to the saints." (2 Corinthians 8:4) Think about that, friends. Most folks dodge a bill, and these people were pleading to get IN on the giving. That's a whole different attitude.

The answer is the Lord. Paul says the Macedonians "…gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us, through the will of God." (2 Corinthians 8:5) The Lord came first, friends. Their giving to Paul's team came after that.

The answer is to help them complete it. Paul says, "…we urged Titus to help complete your act of grace, just as he had started it." (2 Corinthians 8:6) He started it, so now he helps them finish it. I know a thing or two about half-done batches, friends, and a finished one is a whole lot nicer.

The answer is giving. Paul writes, "…see that you also excel in this grace of giving." (2 Corinthians 8:7) The Corinthians already had the faith, the speech and the knowledge covered, friends. Giving is one more thing to add to the list.
The answer is True. Paul says, "I am not giving a command…" (2 Corinthians 8:8) He isn't barking orders, friends. He's inviting them to show how real their love is.

The answer is the sincerity of their love. Paul says, "…I am testing the sincerity of your love through the earnestness of others." (2 Corinthians 8:8) He isn't handing down an order, friends. He's checking whether their love is the real thing, and love that's real shows up in what we do.

The answer is so through His poverty they might become rich. Paul says, "…though He was rich, yet for your sake He became poor, so that you through His poverty might become rich." (2 Corinthians 8:9) He did it for their sake, friends. And Paul calls it the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ.

The answer is finish. Paul says, "Now finish the work, so that you may complete it with the same eager desire, according to your means." (2 Corinthians 8:11) The Corinthians started strong last year, friends. Now it's time to cross the finish line.

The answer is what a person has. Paul says, "…if the eagerness is there, the gift is acceptable according to what one has, not according to what he does not have." (2 Corinthians 8:12) Nobody has to give what they don't have, friends. A small gift with a willing heart counts.

The answer is equality. Paul says, "It is not our intention that others may be relieved while you are burdened, but that there may be equality." (2 Corinthians 8:13) The aim is a fair balance, friends. He doesn't want one side carrying all of it.

The answer is that their surplus will meet Corinth's need. Paul says, "…your surplus will meet their need, so that in turn their surplus will meet your need." (2 Corinthians 8:14) It goes both ways, friends. Today one side gives, and later the other side can.

The answer is False. Paul quotes, "He who gathered much had no excess, and he who gathered little had no shortfall." (2 Corinthians 8:15) So the little gatherer still had no shortfall, friends. And the big gatherer had no excess, so it came out even.
